summary: chai-leaf executes a 3.5MB obfuscated payload at require time while impersonating the pino logger
details: Package chai-leaf@1.4.7 is published under an unrelated description ('vulnerabilities management document') but its tarball ships the pino logger's README, LICENSE, docs/, index.d.ts, and lib/*.js verbatim (references to pinojs/pino, version metadata 9.6.0 in lib/meta.js). The package main index.js unconditionally executes `require('./lib/config')`, which is a single-line ~3.5MB obfuscator.io-style bundle (rotated string-array decoder, self-defending RegExp check, hex-encoded property access, ~20,708-entry string array) containing a shell-execution primitive (execSync). This file does not exist in the real pino project and is not documented anywhere in the package. Any consumer that imports chai-leaf as a logger runs the opaque payload at load time. The combination of legitimate-project impersonation, an undocumented obfuscated internal module auto-loaded by main, and an embedded shell-execution primitive is a supply-chain dropper delivering attacker-controlled code to installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
